primarySuggestion.name: Ductile (spheroidal graphite) iron GJS500-7
primarySuggestion.reasoning: Part is a steering knuckle — a suspension/drivetrain component subjected to high cyclic loads. Combined with the cast_and_machine forced process and 200,000 units/year volume, this profile matches standard automotive practice: sand or high-pressure sand-moulded ductile iron casting followed by CNC finish machining of bores and mating faces. Ductile iron offers the strength/fatigue performance needed for a knuckle at a fraction of steel forging cost, and is far more consistent with the wall-thickness/undercut profile here than aluminium (no HPDC-thin-wall or lightweighting signal present).

processRecommendations.reasoning: User-forced process; geometry (52 undercuts, non-uniform thick sections, 3 machining setups, 14 holes) is classic near-net sand-cast knuckle with post-machining of bores/pads.

manufacturabilityRisks.description: 52 undercut faces relative to a single draw direction will require side-cores/slides in the sand tooling or multiple machining re-orientations.
manufacturabilityRisks.suggestion: Consolidate undercuts onto fewer mould-parting directions or design them as post-cast machined features to simplify the pattern/core-box.

manufacturabilityRisks.description: 102 faces show zero draft, which will cause pattern sticking and core damage during sand-mould stripping, raising scrap and rework.
manufacturabilityRisks.suggestion: Add minimum 1–3° draft to all non-critical faces before pattern release.

manufacturabilityRisks.description: Minimum wall of 1.36mm is well below the safe fill thickness for ferrous sand casting (typically 4–6mm), risking cold-shuts, misruns or porosity.
manufacturabilityRisks.suggestion: Increase local minimum wall to ≥4mm or add ribbing instead of thin unsupported webs.

manufacturabilityRisks.description: Large bores need generous as-cast machining stock and tight post-machining tolerance/finish for bearing seating.
manufacturabilityRisks.suggestion: Cast bores 2–3mm undersize on diameter and finish-bore in a single fixtured operation to hold concentricity.

manufacturabilityRisks.description: Free-form blends increase pattern/core CNC-machining cost and complicate CMM inspection.
manufacturabilityRisks.suggestion: Simplify blends to standard fillet radii where not load-critical.

analysis.aiExplanation: This is a right-hand steering knuckle — a safety-critical suspension component. The sparse fill ratio (0.0615) combined with thick, non-uniform walls (1.36–46.75mm), 52 undercuts, and a mix of cylindrical bores/bosses (bearing seat, ball-joint and tie-rod bores) is fully consistent with a near-net sand-cast ductile-iron part that is subsequently CNC-machined on 3 setups to finish bores, mounting pads and threaded holes. Given the load-bearing, drivetrain-adjacent nature of the part and no aluminium/thin-wall HPDC signal, ductile iron (GJS500/600) is recommended over aluminium, in line with real-world steering knuckle production practice. At 200,000 units/year, high-throughput green-sand or shell-moulding lines with a durable metal pattern (£17k) are economically favoured over die costs for HPDC/forging.
analysisLimitations: Material (ductile iron vs steel forging vs aluminium) is inferred from part type and geometry signals, not from explicit metadata — treat as medium confidence.
Cavity count and pattern life are rule-of-thumb estimates for a high-volume automotive sand-casting line, not derived from OCCT geometry.
Cost range assumes UK labour rates and standard sand-casting + 3-axis/5-axis finish machining; actual costs will vary with supplier tooling amortisation strategy.

dfmIssues.description: Non-uniform sections (heavy:thin ≈ 34.4:1) — Heavy sections solidify last and shrink, drawing porosity/sink at the hot spot.
dfmIssues.fix: Even out wall thickness, core out heavy bosses, add fillets to taper transitions, or feed the hot spot with a riser/chill.

dfmIssues.description: Draft -1° below recommended 0.5° — Insufficient draft galls the die/pattern, raises ejection force and accelerates tool wear (or breaks the sand mould).
dfmIssues.fix: Add ≥ 0.5° draft on all as-cast vertical walls; deep pockets need more. Investment casting can run near-zero draft if this is fixed.

  • What is this part made of? — A CAD file carries shape, not substance. We measured 356 cm³ exactly, but the same solid weighs 0.96 kg in aluminium and 2.79 kg in steel. Nothing in the geometry distinguishes them, and guessing wrong moves the material cost several-fold.
